#CPI数据来袭能否触发9月加息 🔥 #CPI Data Is Here—Will the September Rate Hike Actually Happen?
Brothers, this CPI could be the single most crucial card for the market before the September Federal Reserve meeting. The market is now re-pricing the interest-rate path.
U.S. August CPI rose 3.4% year over year and 0.4% month over month; core CPI was up 2.4% year over year and 0.3% month over month. Inflation pressure hasn’t fully disappeared yet.
Especially on the energy side: gasoline prices increased 3.9% over the month. Oil prices have also strengthened again due to geopolitical conflicts, which means there is a risk of a second spike in inflation later on.
So what the market is truly worried about isn’t just whether there will be a hike in September, but whether the Fed will signal “continued tightening.”
Once rate-hike expectations keep heating up, the dollar and U.S. Treasury yields could strengthen in tandem, putting pressure on BTC, ETH, and highly valued assets in the U.S. stock market.
Conversely, if core inflation continues to cool afterward, the market may shift to trading “tightening nearing its end,” giving risk assets room to breathe.
My take: If CPI comes in hotter than expected, it’s short-term bearish for BTC. But if it’s only a one-off inflation disruption, it doesn’t necessarily mean the entire trend turns bearish.
Next, focus on three key indicators: core CPI, the U.S. dollar index, and real Treasury yields.
If all three move higher at the same time, it will be noticeably harder for BTC to push higher. If the dollar and real rates turn down, that’s the real bullish signal.
So this time, don’t just stare at the CPI number—what the market is trading is how hawkish the Fed’s next move will be.

🔍 Clearpool bets on XRP chain credit: a new DeFi lending story—or just another cold-start dilemma?

💡 First, judge: In the short term, it’s unlikely to meaningfully affect the XRP price. Over the medium term, it depends on whether real borrowing volume can truly take off. I’m giving XRP chain credit a three-month observation period.

📊 Key data
- According to an official announcement, Clearpool will restructure its token model, aiming to enter the credit lending market on the XRP Ledger
- XRP current price: $1.36, up 1.39% in 24h; the news did not trigger any obvious capital movement
- BTC $77,304.01 (+0.62%), ETH $2,513.05 (+2.46%): the broader market environment is stable

📝 Analysis
**1. Institutional credit is the hardest nut to crack in DeFi**
What Clearpool is doing isn’t overcollateralized lending—it’s credit-based lending, where borrowers get funds based on their qualifications rather than collateral. In plain terms, it’s the on-chain version of corporate bonds. Maple and Goldfinch have both stumbled on this road: one wave of bad debts can wipe out half a year’s reputation. This time, moving to the XRP Ledger is a fresh technical story, but none of the commercial-model traps are absent.

**2. Why choose XRP Ledger**
XRP Ledger’s fees and settlement speed really do suit high-frequency, small-ticket lending. And the XRP community’s capital stickiness is strong, effectively bringing along a batch of potential liquidity providers. One sentence translation: Clearpool isn’t selling technology—it’s betting that the XRP ecosystem will finally have a “real DeFi use case” narrative. But whether that narrative becomes monetizable depends on whether institutional borrowers truly want to come.

**3. Token restructuring is a double-edged sword**
Changes to tokenomics often come with expectations of selling pressure in the short term. Long-time holders will immediately ask, “Has my allocation been diluted?” After the announcement, the price only moved 1.39%, suggesting the market is watching from the sidelines—no FOMO, no panic.

💡 Conclusion
Direction call: If, within three months, XRP chain credit can get TVL/borrowing volume into the top 15 on-chain lending rankings, then at the $1.36 level, XRP has a rationale for a rebound/upside follow-through. If within 60 days borrowing volume is still stuck at the demo stage, then this narrative is effectively dead, and XRP will revert to a beta move that tracks the broader market. If I’m wrong, go easy on me—I’m only watching the on-chain data with a small position, not going all-in on the narrative bet.

What do you think—can the XRP ecosystem really produce a DeFi killer app this time?

🔍 Clearpool押注XRP链上信贷：DeFi借贷新故事，还是又一个冷启动难题？

💡 判断先行：短期对XRP价格影响有限，中期看真实借款量能不能起来，我给XRP链上信贷三个月观察期。

📊 核心数据
- 据官方公告，Clearpool将对代币模型进行重构，目标切入XRP Ledger链上信用借贷市场
- XRP现价 $1.36，24h涨1.39%，消息未引发明显资金异动
- BTC $77,304.01（+0.62%）、ETH $2,513.05（+2.46%），大盘环境平稳

📝 分析
**一、机构信贷是DeFi里最难啃的骨头**
Clearpool做的不是超额抵押借贷，是信用借贷，借款人凭资质而非抵押物拿钱。说白了就是链上版的公司债，Maple、Goldfinch都在这条路上摔过跤，坏账一波就能打掉半年口碑。这次换到XRP Ledger，技术上是新故事，商业模式的坑一个没少。

**二、为什么选XRP Ledger**
XRP Ledger的费用和结算速度确实适合高频小额信贷，而且XRP社区的资金粘性强，相当于自带一批潜在流动性提供者。一句话翻译：Clearpool不是在卖技术，是在赌XRP生态终于要有“真正的DeFi用例”这个叙事。但叙事能不能变现，要看机构借款人是否真愿意来。

**三、代币重构是双刃剑**
代币经济学改动短期往往伴随抛压预期，老持有者会先问“我的份额被稀释了吗”。公告后价格只动1.39%，说明市场在观望，没有FOMO也没有恐慌。

💡 结论
方向判断：XRP链上信贷若三个月内TVL/借款量能进入链上借贷前15，$1.36这个位置的XRP有补涨逻辑；如果60天内借款量还停留在演示阶段，这个叙事直接作废，XRP回归跟随大盘的贝塔行情。说错轻喷，我自己也就小仓位盯着链上数据观察，没打算重仓赌叙事。

你怎么看，XRP生态这次真能跑出DeFi杀手级应用吗？

ETH trading volume of $16 billion reversing to outperform BTC; this overnight rebound has something

The overnight script is simple: BTC dipped to 76,000.3, the daily buy zone at 75,507 held (it didn’t break), then it bounced back to 77,236, up 0.34%. As long as the low doesn’t break, the panic from overnight is just paper tiger. But this increase is honestly a bit awkward—alive is good, but don’t expect it to really “work.”

The real signal is in ETH. In the past 24 hours, it’s up +2.13%: it pulled back from 2,433.04 to 2,511, with trading volume of $16.01 billion, pushing past BTC’s $15.93 billion by sheer force. A $16B turnover isn’t something that retail can “kick-start” with a few coins here and there—it’s big money moving seats. Even better: the funding rate is still in negative territory. It rose more than two points on leverage and still didn’t cause people to get carried away/head over heels—this kind of rebound is far more solid than those “inflated” rebounds where funding is fully maxed out.

Now take a look at BTC—it looks a bit miserable: funding rate at +0.006% is positive; longs are paying to prop it up, but the price can’t lift its head below the pivot at 77,683.73. The crowd that got rejected after touching the overnight high of 79,859.8 is still up on the mountaintop, blowing the wind and waiting for a break-even.

BNB is up 1.70% to 727.35, holding steadily above the pivot at 725.19—pretty straightforward, not dragging. XRP is up 1.01% to 1.3573, with 1.42 above and 1.30 below; it keeps acting as background scenery—the main storyline doesn’t revolve around it.

Yesterday around 76,000, how many people shouted that the sky was falling. Today it bounces back and they’re already chasing to ask whether they can still get on. Retail sentiment is always about half a beat faster than the market, and wallets are always half a beat slower. This rhythm hasn’t changed in over a decade.

Direction: slightly bullish, but the small red flowers are only handed out to the “student representatives” of ETH.

For BTC to prove itself, it first needs to reclaim 77,683.73 before it has any right to touch 79,367.17. The data is right there, the direction is given, the price levels are given—what’s left is execution.

According to Crypto Briefing, Chinese AI chip makers have raised prices by as much as 50% due to a shortage of high-bandwidth memory (HBM). The cost of AI compute is being pushed up across the board.

Event overview

Simply put: AI is booming, and there isn’t enough HBM memory needed to build AI chips. Chinese chip makers have raised prices—up to 50%. Chips get more expensive → servers get more expensive → AI company bills get more expensive → global competition for compute power intensifies.

One-sentence translation: Compute power is becoming a scarce asset—whoever has the hardware and electricity holds the voice.

In-depth interpretation

Why is this news important?

On the surface, it’s a supply-chain issue; at its core, it’s an arms race for AI compute power entering a stage of hardware scarcity. When chips rise 50% and there are still buyers, it shows demand hasn’t truly been satisfied.

The transmission to the crypto market is direct: Bitcoin mining and AI data centers are competing for the same pool of electricity and the same type of high-performance hardware. Over the years, mining companies have been bulk shifting toward AI compute hosting (for example, the proportion of AI-related revenue for some listed miners keeps rising). Higher hardware prices mean a revaluation of miners’ assets that positioned early—an angle the market may be overlooking.

Also, rising compute costs will strengthen the narrative of “digital scarcity.” BTC is precisely the hardest digital scarce asset on Earth, and this kind of analogy is a sentiment positive.

In the short term, BTC is currently $77,823.43 (24h -1.30%), ETH $2,461.81 (-0.95%), and altcoins are broadly down (BNB -4.38%, XRP -3.35%). This suggests the market is in a risk-reduction phase, and today this news can’t move the price action.

But in the medium term, if AI capital expenditures continue to exceed expectations, the market’s liquidity narrative may shift from “rate-cut driven” to “tech boom driven,” which is generally supportive for risk assets. Looking at the positive correlation between the 2023–2024 AI theme and BTC, it’s likely that heat from the compute-power sector will spill over into the crypto market.

Anuncios de tasas de interés, reportes de inflación o decisiones regulatorias generan sacudidas violentas en el mercado cripto. Intentar adivinar la dirección del precio minutos antes de una noticia suele terminar en desastre. Sin embargo, el Futures Grid en modo Neutral no necesita predecir hacia dónde irá el mercado, solo necesita que el precio se mueva dentro de un rango determinado.

Es la estrategia preferida por traders cuantitativos para monetizar la volatilidad bidireccional sin sesgo direccional.

1. La Mecánica del Futures Grid Neutral

A diferencia de un Grid Long o Short, el modo Neutral inicia sin posiciones abiertas de compra o venta:

Órdenes de Compra por Debajo: Coloca automáticamente órdenes límite de compra en los niveles inferiores del rango actual.

Órdenes de Venta por Encima: Coloca órdenes límite de venta (corto) en los niveles superiores del rango.

Ejecución Bidireccional: Si el mercado hace un latigazo hacia abajo y luego rebota con fuerza hacia arriba (muy común durante noticias), el bot primero ejecuta compras con descuento y luego las cierra con beneficio en la subida, o viceversa.

Apalancamiento Bajo (2x a 3x): Mantén el apalancamiento al mínimo para absorber velas de mecha larga sin comprometer la liquidez de tu margen.

Rango Amplio: Define un límite inferior y superior con mayor distancia del precio actual (un 5% a 10% de holgura) para evitar que una mecha violenta rompa tu grilla de inmediato.

Margen Aislado: Asigna un capital específico para la estrategia y protégelo de eventos sistémicos usando Stop Loss preestablecidos.

According to a notice from Jin10 about Broadcom (AVGO), as of August 2, its remaining performance obligations (RPO) for the semiconductor and infrastructure software business is about $179.2 billion. In simple terms: customers have already signed contracts and paid, but Broadcom has not delivered yet—those orders have piled up to nearly $180 billion.

One-sentence translation: The arms race in AI infrastructure is still intensifying—the money gets locked into the supply chain first.

The weight of this number lies in the fact that RPO is contracted, deterministic revenue—not a PowerPoint fantasy. A backlog at the scale of hundreds of billions indicates that hyperscale cloud customers (like Google and Meta—this batch of big clients) have truly cast votes with real money for compute demand over the next 3–5 years. This is the same chain of logic as Nvidia’s earnings: the AI capex cycle hasn’t peaked. And the link between this chain and crypto is that the US stock market’s AI narrative is the overall valve for risk appetite this round. As long as AI stocks don’t fall apart, the channel for liquidity to spill over into BTC remains open.

💡 Impact outlook: bullish 📈

- Bias: bullish, expecting an upswing

This kind of hard data gives tech-stock bulls a sense of reassurance, benefiting risk assets overall. ETH is hovering around $2,467.69. If the US stock AI chain strengthens and drives a Nasdaq rebound, ETH’s upside elasticity is usually greater than BTC’s. But to be blunt, this is second-order transmission—not direct buying pressure. As Iran’s domestic economic crisis deepens, questions are being raised about the regime’s stability, and geopolitical risk is being repriced.

According to Crypto Briefing, Iran’s economic crisis has further worsened due to regional conflicts and rising fuel prices, and the market has started discussing the possibility of political unrest—even a change in leadership. Put simply: runaway inflation + skyrocketing cost of living for the public + external conflict—all three mountains are pressing down at once. At the moment, BTC is at $77,946 (24h -1.42%), ETH is $2,467.39, and the market hasn’t fully priced in this risk yet.

Iran’s crisis → if it escalates into political instability → fuel prices surge → inflation expectations heat up → funds look for a risk-off exit beyond fiat. Historically, BTC has shown a track record of rising alongside oil prices in similar scenarios. Also, Iranians have long had demand to use fiat to buy crypto as a hedge against value erosion; a collapse in the rial’s credibility would directly convert into crypto purchasing power.

One-sentence translation: Another country with problems in the fiat system is sending real demand into the crypto world.

- Short term: BTC is consolidating near $77,946, and the sentiment side geopolitical premium hasn’t been fully priced in yet. If the situation escalates, first watch whether the resistance zone at 78,500–79,000 can be pushed through by risk-off capital; ETH will follow, but with weaker elasticity.
- Medium term: A regime change is a low-probability, high-impact event. If it happens, oil prices plus the risk-off bid would jointly drive, and the “fiat alternative” narrative for crypto would be retold. If it doesn’t happen, this news is just noise.

My take
I’m cautiously bullish, with roughly a 60% level of confidence. The logic is simple: at a crisis level like Iran’s, regardless of whether the regime stays stable, the demand for domestic capital to flee is certain—and this portion will keep flowing into BTC. Watch $76,000 support below; if it holds, it’s still within a long-biased structure. If I’m wrong, please just be gentle—I’m expressing my view with a small position. 📰 Why phishing emails can be sent using the official Trezor email address? This time, it’s not a hacker stealing accounts—it's the supply chain that was compromised

💡 Impact on judgment: Neutral. It doesn’t change the BTC trend in the short term, but the warning level for personal asset security is very high.

According to a report by Bitcoin.com, on September 9–10, the customer email systems of three hardware wallet and tax platform providers—Trezor, Bitbox, and Cointracking—were breached. The “security notifications” sent from their official email accounts were actually phishing traps. Bitbox explicitly stated that it’s not a single company that was hacked, but multiple Bitcoin-related companies that were targeted at the same time.

One-sentence translation: The hackers didn’t break into your wallet—they hijacked the wallet manufacturer’s voice, using an official identity to trick you into handing over information.

Deep analysis

Why is this important? The hardware wallet industry sells the concept of “trust.” When phishing emails are sent from a trezor.com official domain, ordinary users’ ability to tell what’s real basically disappears. Moreover, the attack surface isn’t the wallet itself—it’s the email service provider in the supply chain. This shows that industry security levels depend on the weakest third party, not the strongest one.

Related: Attacks targeting custody and identity have been escalating in recent years, and the logic is consistent—if they can’t attack private keys, they attack “people and processes.” BTC is now $77,908 (24h -1.52%), ETH $2,465.77. This kind of news has limited impact on price; it’s more like chronic friction, gradually raising the psychological entry barrier for beginners.

- Asset: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Neutral (slightly bearish on sentiment)
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

💡 My view: This isn’t a sell-off event. Over the next 12 hours, BTC will most likely continue to follow the broader market macro rhythm, and this news won’t independently change direction. If it turns out later that users’ assets were actually stolen—amounting to tens of millions of dollars—then the nature of the event would shift from a “warning” to a “bearish negative,” and that judgment would be invalidated and reassessed.

Verifiable implication: If, in the next few days, it’s confirmed there’s no actual loss of assets, the market will fully digest this news. The support around $77,900 will hold as long as it isn’t broken.

If I’m wrong, don’t be too harsh—these kinds of security incidents, I generally only guard and not move positions.

📰 Putin Warns of Europe Conflict Risk, Why Has BTC $77,282 Not Fallen Yet? This Bearish Move Took a Detour

According to Crypto Briefing, Putin issued a warning to European countries about deploying troops to Ukraine, directly naming the countries that could potentially trigger a wider NATO–Russia conflict. Geopolitical risk is rising, but BTC is currently $77,282.45, up 0.68% over the past 24 hours. ETH $2,513.53 is up 2.52%. Safe-haven signals and market reaction are clearly diverging.

💡 Impact Outlook: Bearish 📉, but the transmission is a slow variable, not a fast one.

In-Depth Analysis

Why is this news important?

Many people think that once a geopolitical conflict starts, BTC should drop immediately—but the transmission path is actually: NATO–Russia conflict risk ↑ → expectations of pressure on European energy prices → sell-off pressure on European risk assets → liquidity contraction in the crypto market → BTC under pressure. This chain takes days to play out, not minutes.

The key lies in Europe’s local capital. Europe is one of the world’s largest hubs for crypto holdings. If conflict expectations escalate, European households and institutions will prioritize pulling liquidity out of risk assets first—BTC and ETH are likely the first to take the hit. ETH $2,513.53’s 2.52% rally is more of a oversold rebound than a trend reversal; if geopolitical news turns bearish again, it will likely give back.

据 CoinTelegraph 报道，链上数据显示比特币卖方风险降至罕见低位，$101.1K附近的抛压基本消失，投资者没有恐慌性抛售，BTC守住了8月大部分涨幅。当前BTC报价 $77,990.34，24h小幅回撤1.37%。

深度解读

为什么重要？

卖方风险指标衡量的是已实现利润/亏损占市值的比例，降到罕见低位意味着：想卖的已经卖完了，剩下的都是拿得住的。说白了就是抛压枯竭。

这个位置很微妙——按市场背景看，ETH $2,468、SOL $101、BNB $717，主流币普跌2-4%，但BTC只跌1.37%抗住了。价差缩窄+卖压枯竭，通常是筹码从弱手换到强手的特征，历史上类似结构往往先于波动率放大出现。

一句话翻译：不是买盘多强，而是卖盘先没脾气了，供给端给多头腾了位置。

对市场的影响

短期：抛压真空期容易走出逼空式反弹，BTC 12小时窗口我偏多，$77,990这个位置只要不放量跌破，反弹概率大于继续下探。

失效条件：如果BTC放量跌破 $77,990.34 区域，抛压枯竭逻辑作废，反而会触发新一批止损盘。

中期：卖方风险低位+横盘，历史上多对应周期底部区域而非顶部，但需要ETF资金面配合验证。

💡 我明确看多这个结构，七成把握，剩下三成交给市场。关注 BTC 能否重新站上 $101.1K 心理位——站上去，套牢盘消失的故事就完整了。说错轻喷，我自己也就小仓位参与。

- 方向：利多📈 预测涨

📰 AI hacker incidents are frequent—what exactly is missing in regulation, and whose responsibility is it anyway, now nobody can say clearly

According to Crypto Briefing, a number of recent “hacker incidents” related to AI have continued to unfold, and experts say these events reveal not a single project’s vulnerabilities, but structural flaws in the entire AI regulatory framework. The core controversy is twofold: who is responsible when something goes wrong (developers/deployers/users), and whether AI systems’ ethical alignment actually has enforceable constraints.

💡 Impact assessment: Neutral. In the short term, this is neither a negative nor a positive for the market—it’s more like a seed that sets up next year’s regulatory agenda.

In-depth analysis

Why it matters

To put it simply, the essence of AI safety is that technology moves faster than rules. As AI agents begin to take over on-chain interactions and automatically sign wallet authorizations, once something goes wrong, the existing legal framework simply doesn’t line up. This isn’t just an AI industry issue—Crypto is the first financial scenario to face large-scale “real-world trials” by AI agents.

One-sentence translation: AI errors aren’t scary—the scary part is that nobody is required to take responsibility.

Market impact

BTC is currently $77,380, trading sideways with 0.2%; ETH is $2,535, up 3%. This news has almost no direct impact on the order book; it’s more of a slow-moving variable.

But note: if regulators use the opportunity to tighten AI agent permissions on-chain (for example, limiting the amount of automatic authorization), the narrative around decentralized AI will first come under pressure. Conversely, if legislation clearly defines responsibility, that would actually be a prerequisite for institutional capital to enter—rules that are clear matter more than rules that are loose.

Trading approach

- Assets: BTC / ETH
- Direction: Neutral (probability is high that BTC will remain within a sideways range over the next 12 hours / ETH will trade around $2,535 within the next 24 hours)
- Rationale: No direct impact on fund flows; purely a regulatory narrative—insufficient price catalyst

💡 My view: Mostly wait and watch. This update doesn’t provide a directional signal. If BTC is hovering above $77,000, don’t乱折腾. A verifiable hypothesis: within the next two weeks, if major economies introduce draft AI responsibility attribution legislation, the related narrative coins will likely see an emotional repricing. Then we can reassess the direction. If BTC breaks below $77,000 on a sustained basis, it suggests the driving force is other variables and this news logic doesn’t hold.

据 Crypto Briefing 报道，近期多起 AI 相关“黑客事件”持续发酵，专家指出这些事件暴露的不是单个项目的漏洞，而是整个 AI 监管框架的结构性缺陷。核心争议两个：出了事责任归谁（开发者/部署方/用户），以及 AI 系统的伦理对齐到底有没有实际约束力。

💡 影响判断：中性。这事短期内既不构成利空也不构成利多，更像是给明年的监管议程埋了个引子。

深度解读

为什么重要

说白了，AI 安全问题的本质是：技术跑得比规则快。AI agent 开始接管链上交互、自动签钱包授权，一旦出事，现行法律框架根本对不上号——这不只是 AI 行业的问题，Crypto 是第一个被 AI agent 大规模“实战”的金融场景。

BTC 现价 $77,380，横盘 0.2%；ETH $2,535，涨 3%。这个新闻对盘面几乎无直接影响，属于慢变量。

但要注意：如果监管借机收紧 AI agent 在链上的权限（比如限制自动授权额度），去中心化 AI 赛道的叙事会先承压。反过来，若立法明确责任归属，反而是机构资金入场的前置条件——规则清晰比规则宽松更重要。

操作思路

- 币种：BTC / ETH
- 方向：中性（BTC 12小时 / ETH 24小时内维持 $77,380 / $2,535 附近震荡的概率大）

💡 我的观点：观望为主。这消息不构成方向性信号，BTC 在 $77,000 上方晃着就别瞎折腾。可验证推论：未来两周内若有主要经济体出台 AI 责任归属草案，相关叙事币种会有一次情绪定价，届时再看方向。如果 BTC 有效跌破 $77,000，那说明驱动盘面的是别的变量，这条新闻的逻辑就不成立。

One-sentence translation: This is the usual play for a small company to borrow a big company’s spotlight—and it doesn’t affect what’s in your wallet.

Just now, Strive said it wanted to buy 500 BTC. Now that the financing is successful, it has added another 178 coins.

Strive raised $630 million via preferred shares to buy 578 BTC. What an impressive bit of accounting.

A couple of days ago, it said Strive wanted to buy 500 BTC; now it has announced a further increase to 578 BTC, relying on a type of preferred-share financing called “SATA.” In plain terms, it issues a bunch of preferred shares to investors, who are paid back with future company earnings or equity rather than taking out a loan directly. It’s a pretty smart move: when Bitcoin rises, Strive’s assets appreciate immediately—more profitable than borrowing money to buy.

At the current $77,332.53 per BTC, buying 578 BTC would cost $4.47 billion in total. The $630 million it raised so far is only the first step; it may need to raise more later. According to CryptoBriefing, this kind of financing could be a new approach to corporate treasury management.

Market impact
- Short term: Bitcoin sentiment may be supported to some extent, since institutions are accumulating coins with a new strategy, signaling optimism. Looking at fund flows, preferred-share buyers seem to value the long-term story more, which could help lower the cost basis of Bitcoin holdings.
- Medium term: If Strive’s model gets copied, corporate coin accumulation could become more common than borrowing to buy, potentially increasing institutional demand for Bitcoin. Regulators may pay attention to this financing instrument and whether it amounts to a form of disguised financial innovation.

My take
This time, I’m bullish on BTC mainly to see whether Strive’s model will work. If it does, there will be more ways for Bitcoin-related companies to finance, and long-term demand could increase. The risk, however, is that preferred-share investors will have to wait a long time to get their money back. If Bitcoin drops too much, they might flip and short Strive instead, which would put additional pressure on Bitcoin. If I’m wrong, go easy on me—I’ll just test it with a small position.

- Asset: BTC
- Direction: Bullish 📈 Predicts a rise
- Duration: 12 hours

Event overview
Put simply: shorts got squeezed together. When price starts rising, leveraged short positions are forcibly liquidated. In this 3.21% bullish candle, a significant portion of the gain is “contributed” by the shorts being liquidated.

A short-squeeze market has two sides: strong short-term momentum, but once the liquidation “fuel” burns out, the rally often gives back because there’s no spot demand to absorb the price. To judge this move’s quality, look at whether ETH can hold above $2,500 over the next 24 hours. Historically, these liquidation-driven pulses typically retrace about half the gain within 24–48 hours after the fuel is exhausted. Invalidation condition: if ETH breaks below $2,542.48 on rising volume, the short-squeeze logic fails and the short-term momentum weakens.

📰 Strive wants to buy 500 BTC—can the route of stock financing to hoard coins actually work?

According to Crypto Briefing, Strive plans to purchase 500 BTC this week, with the funding coming from preferred share issuance. At the current $77,218, this is about $38.6 million.

💡 Impact assessment: Positive for the short and mid term; within 12 hours BTC could see a sentiment-driven rebound.

Put simply, this is another follower of the MicroStrategy playbook: a listed company raises capital using financial instruments and stuffs its balance sheet with BTC. The difference is that Strive is using preferred shares—fixed dividends, which must be paid. That means it has less tolerance for BTC price fluctuations than the MSTR model with convertible bonds: if the coin price trades sideways, it still has to pay dividends; if the coin price drops sharply, it faces pressure from both sides.

One-sentence translation: Another listed company has chosen to become a leveraged buyer of BTC—short term it’s buy pressure, but long term it adds a potential risk trigger.

Why does it matter? Right now, BTC is ranging around $77,218, with only +0.12% over 24h. What the market lacks is incremental buying. Although 500 BTC isn’t that much (spot-market volume over just a few minutes), the signal is more important than the capital itself—it confirms that the “corporate coin-hoarding funding channel” is still working. Reference MSTR’s path: announcement → issuing shares at a premium → buying coins → positive feedback between the stock price and the coin price. Strive is smaller; whether this works depends on how hot the preferred-share subscription is. If the issuance is lukewarm, the whole logic falls apart.

Impact on ETH is limited. ETH at $2,546.34 is up +3.31% today, showing stronger performance and moving to its own rhythm.

My view: Slightly bullish in the short term. If $77,218 holds steady, the combination of corporate buying and ETH strength makes it more likely that within 12 hours price tests the upside resistance. I’ll give it a 70% probability; the remaining 30% I leave to the market. If I’m wrong, go easy on me—I’m only backing it with a small position. If the preferred-share issuance fails or is delayed, the short-term bullish thesis instantly invalidates; if BTC breaks below $77,218, it would mean the “corporate hoarding” narrative can’t hold the order book anymore—don’t get stuck fighting it.

Events like this push hardware wallet manufacturers to implement DKIM verification and anti-phishing codes, making the industry’s infrastructure more robust. Historically, Trezor’s email disclosures have happened multiple times, and each time the price foundation of the coins was not harmed.

Neutral event; it doesn’t constitute a directional basis. This is a security incident, not a funds incident—no coins were stolen, and no exchanges were hacked. - Medium term: If ETH can hold above $2,577, the liquidation zone could become support. The switch in sentiment—from short to long—would only be confirmed once that happens.

My take
I’m bullish on the upside. I also think the short squeeze in ETH still has momentum, and in the next 24 hours it’s likely to strengthen further. But you need to distinguish: an upswing driven by liquidations is not the same as one driven by genuine buying. The former moves fast but isn’t solid. 📰 Stablecoins break through $30 billion— is the US dollar hegemony being strengthened, or sidelined?

According to Crypto Briefing, the total market capitalization of stablecoins has surpassed $300 billion. The article’s core contradiction is intriguing: stablecoins both reinforce the dollar’s global currency status and plant the seeds of systemic risk. In plain terms, everyone is using on-chain “dollar” instruments, but no one controls what happens if something goes wrong.

Why is this news important?
What does $300 billion mean? This is no longer just self-congratulation within the Crypto community—it’s a parallel offshoot of the global dollar system. The fundamental logic is: emerging markets have long had a demand for the dollar, while traditional SWIFT channels are slow and expensive; stablecoins happen to be the smoothest alternative. For every USDT/USDC minted, an equivalent amount of Treasuries or cash is locked behind it—meaning global users are effectively “booking” bids for Treasuries.

Regulatory trends are moving in the same direction. Last year, the U.S. stablecoin legislative approach was essentially “embrace them but regulate them,” which sharply contrasts with the crackdown on altcoins. Stablecoins sit in a more regulation-friendly position—this is a structural reason why capital keeps flowing into this cycle.

Market impact
In the short term, stablecoin market cap expansion = more off-exchange funding ammunition, which is a direct tailwind for BTC $78,736.01 and ETH $2,611.31. ETH’s 24h gain of 6.94% today is partly explained by this: stablecoins are mainly issued on ETH and L2s. The larger the market cap, the more value ETH as the settlement layer captures.

Just as BTC buy orders disappeared, how did it rebound directly back to $78,812 after the CPI landed?

💡 Positive: A CPI downside surprise turned into the starting gun for a rebound—BTC is expected to trade stronger (range-bound) over the next 12 hours

In my previous post, we talked about spot demand collapsing into negative—then the plot reversed. According to Binance Square, after the CPI was released, BTC surged violently from a low of $76,046, at one point jumping to $79,301.

One sentence to make it clear
The key CPI didn’t smash the market—BTC rebounded instead. Bad news landing = buyers returning.

What’s going on
Core CPI for August was up 0.3% month-on-month, higher than the expected 0.2%, and annualized to about 3.7%—the only item that missed in the whole report. By right, that should be bearish and BTC should fall. But the opposite happened: after the spike to $76,046, a V-shaped reversal followed. In 24 hours it’s up 2.68%, and it briefly reclaimed $79,301; it has since pulled back to $78,812.9.

One-line translation: The data itself is bearish, but the market priced in the bad news long ago. When it finally landed, there was no new sell pressure—so shorts were instead squeezed.

Market impact
- Short term: Bearish news landing → risk appetite rebounds. This transmission is straightforward: CPI didn’t “blow up,” meaning the November rate-cut expectations weren’t completely killed. The macro liquidity narrative is still alive, and funds are willing to flow back into risk assets. ETH even rose 6.66% in 24 hours to $2,602.72. The rebound strength is stronger than BTC’s, suggesting this move wasn’t BTC-only—it's a broad market risk-on.
- Medium term: Core inflation stickiness remains. The Fed’s rate-cut pace may be slower, so the rebound height could be capped. Don’t expect it to rocket back in one go.

My view
I’m moderately bullish, but only for a short-term up move. The logic is simple: that wick at $76,046 was the short-term bottom signal. Even with bad CPI data, the bears couldn’t push it down—meaning the selling pressure is exhausted. First watch whether it can hold above $79,300; if it holds, there will be room for further upside. The risk is that the figure of core CPI annualized at 3.7% won’t just disappear—if Fed officials turn hawkish afterward, the rebound could be cut short at any time. 📰 ZEC plunges more than 10% in a single day, breaks $1,100: how did the PPI data “turn privacy coins back into their former selves”?

According to Bitcoin.com, on Friday Zcash (ZEC) fell below $1,100, with a daily drop of more than 10%, and its market cap slipped back to $18.5 billion. The trigger was that U.S. PPI data came in above expectations, causing an overall pullback in the crypto market—altcoins were hit first.

💡 Impact assessment: bearish. In the short term, altcoins are likely to face continued pressure, while BTC $77,878 (down only -1.17% in 24h) is clearly more resilient than altcoins.

In-depth analysis

Why is this news important?

Plainly put, this move in ZEC isn’t really about ZEC itself—it’s a ranking race when liquidity retreats. PPI above expectations → inflation worries flare up → expectations for rate cuts get pushed back → high-beta assets get sold first. Privacy coins, which are purely narrative-driven and low-liquidity, surge on FOMO when they rise—yet when they fall, there’s nobody queuing up to buy.

The data makes it very clear: BTC fell just 1.17% over 24h, ETH is down 3.80%, SOL is down 2.21%, while ZEC is down in double digits. Money isn’t leaving the market; it’s being withdrawn from fringe assets back into core assets. In one sentence: this isn’t a bear market signal—it’s a signal that risk appetite is contracting.
